dedupe_keys.name: flood damage models for rice inventory and data driven models for thailand and myanmar

description: A set of flood damage models for rice crops with an inventory of published models. The Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences paper (published 26 February 2026) reviews 20 damage models from 12 countries and builds empirical models from survey data in Thailand and Myanmar, including deterministic and probabilistic stage-damage functions, Bayesian regression and random forest, using water depth, flood duration and growth stage, and tests transfer between regions; random forest was most accurate. The inventory with lookup tables is free on the NTU data repository (doi 10.21979/N9/OZGWXE) and the models are on GitHub; the paper is CC BY 4.0. Coverage is Thailand and Myanmar for the new models and 12 countries for the inventory. Caveats: transferring models to new regions adds error, as the paper shows. For simulation it gives rice loss functions for flood risk models of farms and food supply. A related catalogue record is the JRC global flood depth-damage functions.
